departments.title: PLAYCRAFT — game design and gameplay quality
departments.summary: Assesses and improves how a game plays. Reads the repo (intent, engine, controls, systems with file:line evidence, genres across 15 genre profiles), plays the built game in Chromium on desktop and phone (response time of every control, dead time, idle motion, FPS, pause, touch targets, text size), scores 10 categories 0-100 with evidence levels (verified / observed / inferred / not tested) and confidence, ranks the highest-impact opportunities by impact, effort and risk, writes a staged plan, then verifies changes against the baseline (regressions + guardrails on the git diff) with a before/after report. full_pass adds GITCRAFT's engineering checks (TestCraft) under one plan.

departments.title: PIXELCRAFT — visual quality, UI/UX and interface efficiency
departments.summary: Audits the rendered application (not its source) in Chromium at iPhone 17, iPhone 13, desktop, narrow, tablet and landscape viewports: discovers its screens, captures screenshots, measures spacing, alignment, typography, touch targets, control consistency, safe areas, overflow, layout shift, hover/pressed/focus/disabled states, runs axe-core and user journeys (taps, depth, confirmations, feedback time). Scores Visual Quality, Usability and Consistency (100 each) from evidence, with coverage and confidence reported separately; every finding has screen, viewport, selector, measurements, severity, an annotated screenshot and a fix. verify replays the same routes, viewports and journeys, diffs screenshots, proves fixes and refuses score gains from lost coverage. Works on React, Vite, Next.js, static sites and browser games (HTML overlays). Never modifies the app.
departments.applies_because: PIXELCRAFT audits the rendered HTML UI of apps, sites and games

departments.title: DESIGNCRAFT — game-design intelligence
departments.summary: levels, missions, story, progression and experience, from the game's own data

findings.title: One story path: no endings, choices or branches in the data
findings.evidence: No ending definitions and no scripted choices were found, although the docs talk about choice or consequence 15 times. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add one decision with two outcomes at the story's midpoint.

findings.title: Only 0 of 35 objectives offer more than one way to complete them
findings.evidence: Almost every objective has exactly one target and one method in its definition. (facts verified in source: 5)
findings.recommendation: Give key objectives a second valid target or method.

findings.title: The player decides how fast, never what or how
findings.evidence: No objective offers alternatives, none is optional, and the story has no endings or choices in the data; free play exists (12 references) but is separate from the missions. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add alternatives and optional goals to the five most-played missions.

findings.title: 'interact' is 37% of all objectives
findings.evidence: 13 of 35 objectives use the verb 'interact'. (facts verified in source: 5)
findings.recommendation: Replace a third of the 'interact' objectives with other actions.

findings.title: 2 missions share the same structure: travel → interact
findings.evidence: Tree Down on the Pass and Stuck in the Drift have an identical sequence of objective types. 2 of 8 missions repeat a structure another mission already uses. (facts verified in source: 2)
findings.recommendation: Give each of Tree Down on the Pass and Stuck in the Drift one objective the others do not have.

findings.title: 20 of 45 named places are never a mission destination
findings.evidence: No mission objective targets Tannberg Base, Fernhut Cabin, Slope A, Slope B, Slope C and 15 more. They exist in the world data but the mission structure never asks the player to go there. (facts verified in source: 6)
findings.recommendation: Route existing missions through the unused places.

findings.title: 5 of 8 missions mention no character
findings.evidence: The briefs, objectives and completion text of Eyes on Kessel Bowl, Controlled Release, Firewood for the Kettle, Tree Down on the Pass and 1 more name none of the 7 characters. (facts verified in source: 5)
findings.recommendation: Put a person in Eyes on Kessel Bowl, Controlled Release and Firewood for the Kettle: who asked, who is helped.

findings.title: 56% of the mapped area holds nothing to find or do
findings.evidence: Dividing the playable extent (1720×1305 units) into a 6×6 grid, 20 cells contain no placed location and no mission target; the emptiest quarter is the north-east (6 of 9 cells empty). (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add landmarks and small finds to the north-east of the map.

findings.title: Buying everything costs 5.1× what the campaign pays
findings.evidence: The non-repeating missions pay 1390 funds in total; the 35 priced unlocks cost 7100. The gap is meant to be filled by 2 repeatable mission(s) (Tree Down on the Pass and Stuck in the Drift). (facts verified in source: 2)
findings.recommendation: Bring prices and income closer: raise campaign rewards or lower top prices.

findings.title: Missions define no way to fail
findings.evidence: No mission definition has a fail condition, time limit or loss state; the source has 12 fail-state references, so failure may live in code outside the mission data. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add a soft fail state to missions with a clock or a threat.

findings.title: No optional or bonus objectives
findings.evidence: None of the 35 objectives is marked optional or bonus. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add one optional bonus objective to each mission.

findings.title: PLAYCRAFT measured 5.1 s from load to first input
findings.evidence: In PLAYCRAFT run 20261105001110-pass-06bc6f6e the game took 5.1 s before it accepted play (software renderer; real devices are usually faster).
findings.recommendation: Let the player act during loading.

departments.title: TestCraft — automated QA
departments.summary: Browser QA for web games with Playwright + Chromium: smoke tests on desktop, phone and tablet emulation (errors, missing files, blank screens, overflow, canvas), scripted gameplay with assertions on game state and video capture, FPS / frame-time / heap profiling, visual regression (YIQ pixel diff, baselines), asset integrity (every file opened by format; GLBs through the Khronos validator; texture budgets), animation playback (GLB clips really move; sprite frames differ), the project's own Vitest/Jest suite, and HTML/JSON reports.

departments.title: AssetCraft — asset management
departments.summary: One asset catalogue for every project (SQLite in ~/.gitcraft/assetcraft): every department run registers its outputs with licence and provenance; scan existing projects; search across projects; versions on content change; exact and perceptual (dHash) duplicates; unused assets (not referenced by source); dependency tracing (glTF, Tiled, HTML/CSS); licence inventory with ATTRIBUTION.md and non-commercial flags; hash re-verification; hash-verified integration into a project (never overwriting silently); 3D-library sync; a browsable HTML catalogue.

conflicts.title: Difficulty: DESIGNCRAFT 10% vs PLAYCRAFT 68%
conflicts.detail: DESIGNCRAFT reads the design data (source); PLAYCRAFT measures the played build. A large gap means the design intent and the played experience disagree. Trust measured play for how it plays today, and the design analysis for what the data allows; confirm in a playtest before acting on either alone.
